# Module `tasks`

tasks - spawn self-contained unit-of-work and await its result.

Unlike the threads module, a task is "fire-and-forget": task_spawn starts the
closure on a detached pthread and immediately returns a task handle. The task
delivers its result to a private capacity-1 channel (the handle *is* that
channel), so the caller decides when to wait:

  task_await(t)  blocks until the value arrives and returns it.
  task_poll(t)   returns Int? -- present holding the result once the task has
                 delivered it, absent while it is still running.
  task_free(t)   reclaims the task handle; returns 0 or -1.

Fallible operations follow the engine-wide `T?` shape (PROGRAMMERS_GUIDE
§3.16): task_spawn returns `Int?` and is absent only when the worker thread or
its result channel could not be created. task_poll is a native `Int?` rather
than the old `-1` sentinel, so a legitimate result of `-1` is no longer
indistinguishable from "not ready". task_await stays a plain Int: on a valid
handle it always blocks until a result arrives (which may be any Int), so it
has no absence to report.

Usage:
  import tasks
  t<Int> = task_spawn(|| -> 40 + 2) else 0
  v = task_await(t)         // 42
  task_free(t)              // Bool? -> present on success

  t2<Int> = task_spawn(|| -> 99) else 0
  while (task_poll(t2) else 0 != 99) { }   // spin until ready
  task_free(t2)

<a id="sym-task_await"></a>
### `task_await` · fn

```
task_await(h<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Block until `task` finishes; returns its closure result. On a valid handle the
result is always delivered (it may be any Int, including -1); only an invalid
handle yields -1.

<a id="sym-task_free"></a>
### `task_free` · fn

```
task_free(h<Int>)<Bool?> ->
```

Reclaim the task handle. Returns `Bool?` -- present on success, absent on a
bad handle.

<a id="sym-task_poll"></a>
### `task_poll` · fn

```
task_poll(h<Int>)<Int?> ->
```

Non-blocking presence check: returns `Int?` -- present holding the result once
the task has delivered a value (the result may legitimately be -1), absent
while the task is still running. Unwrap with `else default` or `match`.

<a id="sym-task_spawn"></a>
### `task_spawn` · fn

```
task_spawn(work<fn() -> Int>)<Int?> ->
```

Start `work` on a detached task thread. Returns `Int?` -- present holding the
task handle (>= 1) on success, absent when the thread or channel could not be
created. The closure must be a plain `fn() -> Int`.
